title: Setup, Object Manager, App Launcher, Lightning Experience, and Mobile
objectives: Navigate Setup to find administrative tools efficiently.
Open Object Manager to inspect schema metadata.
Use App Launcher to switch apps and items in Lightning Experience.
Recognize how mobile access relates to the same org metadata and data.
diagnostic_question: A new admin needs to add a picklist value and verify it on a mobile phone. Which UI areas do they use—in what order—and what is metadata vs runtime verification?
definition: Setup is where administrators customize the org. In Lightning Experience, most object customizations—fields, page layouts, and related settings—are available from Object Manager in Setup ([Find Object Management Settings](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=extend_click_find_objectmgmt_parent.htm)). The App Launcher is how users open Lightning apps; Help documents opening apps from App Launcher in Lightning Experience and the Salesforce mobile app ([Lightning Usage App](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.lex_lightning_usage_app.htm); [Vertical Navigation](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.base_vertical_nav.htm)). Page layouts also control how record detail pages, fields, and actions appear in the Salesforce mobile app, and Lightning Experience can display page-layout elements differently than Classic ([Page Layouts](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.customize_layout.htm)). Exact header icons and click paths are release-sensitive—Needs verification in the target org.
why_it_matters: Admins who cannot navigate Setup waste time and misconfigure the wrong area. Lightning and mobile are how users experience metadata decisions.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a hotel. Setup is the back-office key cabinet. Object Manager is the room-type catalog—beds, phones, and door locks for each room type. App Launcher is the elevator directory of floors (Lightning apps). Lightning Experience is the guest lobby on a desktop. Mobile is the in-room tablet: same hotel, smaller tray, and some buttons look different, so you verify the tablet instead of assuming lobby parity.
deeper_explanation: Quick Find lets you navigate to a Setup page by keyword, and the result list narrows as you type. ([Setup and Object Manager Tips](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/setup-quick-look/learn-to-use-setup-and-the-object-manager))

Object Manager lists standard and custom objects and exposes related settings from one entry point. ([Setup and Object Manager Tips](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/setup-quick-look/learn-to-use-setup-and-the-object-manager))

For a field change, the supported learning path is Setup → Object Manager → object → Fields & Relationships; a record edit changes data in one record, not the field definition. ([Enhance Salesforce Data Entry Customization](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/projects/customize-a-salesforce-object/standard-custom-fields))

A Lightning app bundles objects, tabs, and other items in a navigation bar, while the App Launcher lets users switch contexts. ([Enhance Efficiency with Custom Lightning Apps](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/lex_customization/lex_customization_apps))

The App Manager exposes whether an app is visible in Lightning Experience, and app assignment or tab settings can limit what a user can reach. ([Enhance Efficiency with Custom Lightning Apps](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/lex_customization/lex_customization_apps) [Manage Salesforce Permissions and Security Settings](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/projects/keep-data-secure-in-a-recruiting-app/fls-perm-sets-sharing))

The Salesforce mobile app provides CRM data on a phone or tablet and reads org metadata, but mobile and desktop can differ in features and display. ([Salesforce Mobile App Benefits & Features](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/salesforce1_mobile_app/salesforce1_mobile_app_intro))

Field-level security controls whether a profile or permission set can view or edit a field and remains enforced regardless of the client; page layouts and Lightning pages control presentation. ([Manage Salesforce Permissions and Security Settings](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/projects/keep-data-secure-in-a-recruiting-app/fls-perm-sets-sharing) [Boost Salesforce Record Page Customization](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/lex_customization/lex_customization_page_layouts))

mental_model.analogy: A hotel: Setup is the back-office key cabinet; Object Manager is the room-type catalog; App Launcher is the elevator directory of Lightning apps; Lightning Experience is the desktop lobby; mobile is the in-room tablet.
where_it_breaks: A tablet is not a guaranteed smaller lobby—Help states Lightning Experience and the mobile app can show page-layout elements differently.
App Launcher visibility can be limited by app assignment and OAuth/app policies; the directory is not a security boundary by itself.
Object Manager in Classic is organized differently than in Lightning Experience—Needs verification of the UI you actually have.
The analogy does not encode field-level security; a field can exist in Object Manager and still be hidden on Lightning or mobile.

worked_example.output: Value is selectable for authorized users on web and mobile when object access, FLS, page/layout presentation, record type, and app/tab assignment allow it.
worked_example.self_explanation: Metadata changed in Setup; user experience confirmed where users actually work.

steps: Open Setup via gear menu; use Setup search to open Object Manager.
Pick any standard object; open Fields & Relationships.
Switch to Sales app via App Launcher; open a list view.
Optional: open Salesforce mobile app or mobile browser; compare navigation.
guided_completion: Name three landmarks: Setup, Object Manager, App Launcher.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Changed context: User cannot see a newly added object tab in App Launcher. Produce a numbered diagnostic: (1) verify the correct org and user, then reproduce in Lightning; (2) check App Manager app assignment and Visible in Lightning; (3) check profile/permission-set Tab Settings and object permissions; (4) if the tab appears but a field is missing, check the page layout/Lightning page and then field-level security; (5) repeat on Salesforce mobile and label a client/display difference versus an access-control failure. Expected sequence is source-backed by SF-APP-LAUNCHER, SF-TAB-VISIBILITY, SF-PAGE-LAYOUT, and SF-FLS. Evidence/feedback criterion: full credit requires an observed result and next action for every step, cites those source IDs, and states that FLS is enforced across clients; feedback names the first failed control instead of blaming the mobile app.
evidence: Screenshot or notes of the navigation path, with the correct org/user context omitted from exported evidence.

Completed changed-context diagnostic with an observed result and next action for app assignment, tab setting/object access, page/layout presentation, and FLS; cite SF-APP-LAUNCHER, SF-TAB-VISIBILITY, SF-PAGE-LAYOUT, and SF-FLS.
hands_on_lab.limitations: Playground apps may differ from enterprise orgs.

flashcards.back: The administrative workspace where you customize, configure, and support the org—not where most users work records.
The Setup hub for standard and custom objects, including fields and page layouts, in Lightning Experience.
The Lightning Experience (and mobile) control that lets users open and switch the apps they are allowed to see.
The modern Salesforce desktop UI where apps, navigation, and record pages are presented to users.

flashcards.front: Where does a sales rep start daily work?

No. Setup is for administrators with permissions such as View Setup and Configuration.

interview_questions.question: How do you navigate Setup to change a field definition?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I open Setup, go to Object Manager, pick the object, then Fields. That changes metadata. Editing one Lightning Experience record only changes that record's data.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help says most object customizations in Lightning Experience live in Object Manager in Setup—fields, page layouts, and related settings. I use Setup search rather than hunting menus. After the save, I still check field-level security and the page layout, then verify in the App Launcher app users actually use, including mobile. Exact gear-icon clicks are release-sensitive, so I verify landmarks in the org instead of memorizing a pixel path.
interview_questions.example: Adding a Partner Referral value to Lead Source is an Object Manager field edit, not typing the words on one Lead record in Lightning Experience.
tradeoffs: Speed of a Setup change versus verifying layouts, FLS, and mobile
follow_ups: How would you prove a non-admin can see it?
weak_answer_warnings: Says to edit a record to change the field definition

interview_questions.question: What is the App Launcher for, and how is it different from Setup?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: App Launcher is how users open Lightning Experience apps they are allowed to see. Setup is the back-office configuration workspace. Most sales users should never live in Setup.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: A Lightning app groups tabs and items. Users switch those apps from App Launcher on desktop and, in documented mobile flows, from the mobile app menu. Assignment and tab settings decide what appears. Setup and Object Manager are administrator surfaces. Confusing the two is a classic interview fail: 'the object is missing' often means the tab is not in the user's app, not that Object Manager deleted it.
interview_questions.example: A service user opens App Launcher, chooses the Service app, and never needs Setup; the admin uses Setup Object Manager to add a Case field.
tradeoffs: Many small apps versus one crowded app
follow_ups: What if the app is missing for one profile?
Does App Launcher grant object permission?
weak_answer_warnings: Treats App Launcher as Setup or as a security boundary

interview_questions.question: A user can see a new field in Lightning Experience but not on the Salesforce mobile app. How do you diagnose?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I split field-level security from page layout and from mobile display. Help says Lightning Experience and the mobile app can show page-layout elements differently, so I test the actual phone client.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: First I confirm the field exists in Object Manager and that FLS allows the profile. FLS is enforced regardless of client. Then I check the page layout and Lightning page on desktop. Then I open the Salesforce mobile app as that user. A missing mobile field is often a compact layout or mobile section, not a failed Setup save. I do not grant Modify All to 'make mobile work.'
interview_questions.example: Lead Source shows Partner Referral on desktop Lightning Experience; the mobile record page omits the field until the page layout's mobile sections include it.
tradeoffs: Desktop-only verification versus testing the real mobile client
follow_ups: Is the field missing on all records or one record type?
weak_answer_warnings: Blames the mobile app as broken without checking layout and FLS

interview_questions.question: A new administrator is lost in Setup. How do you teach landmarks without a click-by-click script?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I teach three landmarks: Setup as back office, Object Manager for objects and fields, App Launcher for user apps in Lightning Experience. Then they search instead of wandering.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Task-based navigation beats a tree tour. To change a field: Setup → Object Manager → object. To see what users see: leave Setup, open App Launcher, pick the Lightning app, open a record, then repeat on mobile. I warn that menu labels move by release. I also show that a missing Setup gear is usually a permission, not a broken laptop. Delegated admin is a later conversation.
interview_questions.example: On day one, the new admin uses Setup search for Object Manager, adds a picklist value, then verifies it through App Launcher in the Sales app.
tradeoffs: Hand-holding versus sending them into an outdated click list
follow_ups: Do they have View Setup and Configuration?
Which disposable org are they in?
weak_answer_warnings: Random walkthrough of every Setup node

interview_questions.question: A custom object tab is missing from a user's App Launcher. What is your path?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I check they are in Lightning Experience, then app assignment, tab settings, and object permissions. App Launcher only shows what that user is allowed to open.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Reproduce as the user. Confirm the object still exists in Object Manager—no tab does not mean no object. Then App Manager or app assignment, tab visibility, and object CRUD. Classic versus Lightning can hide different things. Mobile has its own navigation. I do not recreate the object. I also do not treat a connected-app OAuth policy as the first guess unless this is an external app in the launcher.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Request__c exists in Object Manager, but the Sales app assignment omitted the tab, so App Launcher never listed it for that profile.
follow_ups: Can an admin see the tab?
Is this Lightning Experience or Classic?

interview_questions.question: The Setup link is missing from the gear menu. What do you check?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I check View Setup and Configuration on the user's profile or permission set, in the correct org, before blaming the browser or Lightning Experience.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: A missing Setup entry is an access-control hypothesis. Standard users should not see Setup. I verify org, user, and the permission name rather than inventing a new privilege. Then I separate that from a Classic versus Lightning Experience difference. Mobile is not the place I expect full Setup. Least privilege means we grant Setup only to people who configure, not to every App Launcher user.
interview_questions.example: A sales manager on a standard profile has App Launcher and Lightning Experience but no Setup gear until a permission set with View Setup and Configuration is assigned for a temporary audit.
tradeoffs: Least privilege versus making every manager an administrator
follow_ups: Delegated administration instead of full Setup?
Are they in a sandbox versus production?
weak_answer_warnings: Tells them to reinstall the browser first

interview_questions.question: Design Lightning apps for three personas in a twenty-person company.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I make focused Lightning Experience apps—Sales, Service, and Ops—with only the tabs each persona needs, assigned so App Launcher stays uncluttered, and I still verify mobile separately.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Personas map to jobs, not to every object in Object Manager. Sales gets Leads and Opportunities; Service gets Cases; Ops gets the custom request object. App Launcher assignment and tab settings enforce that. Setup stays admin-only. I document overlap objects like Account. I test each app on Lightning Experience desktop and on the Salesforce mobile app because layouts can differ. I do not ship one mega-app that dumps every tab on everyone.
interview_questions.example: Twenty people: Sales app for six reps, Service app for four agents, Ops app for two coordinators; admins still use Setup Object Manager behind the scenes.
tradeoffs: Overlap of Account on every app versus clutter
follow_ups: Who owns app assignment after go-live?
weak_answer_warnings: One app containing every object for every user

interview_questions.question: Explain Setup versus Lightning Experience to a sales manager without jargon.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Lightning Experience plus App Launcher is the lobby where you work customer records. Setup is the back office where administrators change the building. You should not need Setup for daily sales work.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use the hotel mapping, then break it. The elevator directory is App Launcher. The lobby is Lightning Experience. The tablet in the room is mobile—it is the same hotel but some buttons differ, so we test the phone. Object Manager is the room-type catalog in the back office. If a field is missing, we do not tell the manager to 'go to Setup'; we check their app, layout, and access. I invite them to show me the record in App Launcher, not to become an administrator.
interview_questions.example: A sales manager who bookmarked Setup is redirected to App Launcher → Sales app → Opportunity, while the admin keeps field changes in Object Manager.
tradeoffs: Empowering managers versus accidentally creating shadow administrators
follow_ups: Should this manager have any Setup permission?
How do they report a missing field?
weak_answer_warnings: Jargon-heavy tour of every Setup node
